## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1,\ j=r-t+1,\ a=\min(n-r-i,r-j),\ b=\min(i,j)\); the lower-adjoined family generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- [source-backed] The transposed/right-adjoined family is \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\), and is the conjugate family. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
- [computed] In the \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,3,3)\) interval, the ten lower-adjoined classes form a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q=J/A_+J\). [artifact 527b9b1cd586e81294f01def5f51d30afb4c5919e505f335d85bd759ec0facf1; artifact fe0114a78a3f2045e7b37abfb47b72bebb85782ac6dc52bc0b3bcf6ce46b3e14]
- [proved] Partition conjugation induces an automorphism of \(Q\), preserves \(A_+J\), and carries the certified lower-adjoined basis to the right-adjoined family.
- [proved] Both specialized ten-element families minimally generate \(J\).

## Strategy
Take
\[
n=10,\quad r=q=5,\quad i=j=2,\quad p=q-i=3,\quad c=r-j=3,
\]
so \(a=3,\ b=2\); equivalently this is \(v_{5,5,4,10}\).
Let
\[
A=\Lambda/I_{5,5},\qquad
J=\bigoplus_{22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^5}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda,
\qquad Q=J/A_+J.
\]
The involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) preserves \(I_{5,5}\), since
\(\lambda\subseteq5^5\iff\lambda'\subseteq5^5\). Hence it descends to \(A\).
It preserves \(J\), since \(22\subseteq\lambda\iff22\subseteq\lambda'\), and preserves degree. Therefore
\[
\omega(A_+J)=\omega(A_+)\omega(J)=A_+J,
\]
so it descends to \(Q\).

The certified lower basis is
\[
L=(22,221,222,2211,2221,22111,2222,22211,22221,22222).
\]
Its conjugate is
\[
\omega(L)=(22,32,33,42,43,52,44,53,54,55)
=\{\bar s_\mu:22\subseteq\mu\subseteq5^2\},
\]
which is precisely the right-adjoined family because
\[
((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})=(5^2).
\]
Thus the right family is also a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q\).

Both families generate \(J\) by the cited generation statements. Applying the accepted indexed-family graded Nakayama criterion to each ten-element generating family whose image is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q\) shows that neither admits a proper generating subfamily.

Status: the requested case-specific \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,3,3)\) two-family minimality target is established.

## Gaps
- This proves only the certified \(i=j=2,\ p=c=3\) case, not an arbitrary-\((i,j)\) assertion with \(p=c=3\).
